hypothesis: The paper's spine is 'a small kernel inside exact BP instead of a large score network'. Three comparisons support it; only two were ever measured on shared data. em_bp vs mdn is E25, on exp34-* bundles. nets vs a frozen E02a em_bp is E28/E29, on exp31-* bundles. mdn vs nets -- the row E25's own registered hypothesis is about ('sits between the unstructured networks and the mixture-innovation EM-BP on the information ladder') -- has never been measured and CANNOT be obtained by reading E25's numbers beside E29's: exp_34 draws under the tags exp34-train/val/test and E03 under exp31-train/val/test, so the two experiments are scored on DIFFERENT DATA, not the same data by different fits. E30 refits BOTH kernel arms on E03's bundles, with E03's corruption interface and E03's estimand, so every arm in the project sits on one axis.
design: Part `ladder`: em_bp (MixtureInnovationKernel, 8 components, initialised rho=0.3 var=0.8 exactly as E25 does so a difference is attributable to the bundles and not to the start) and mdn (MDNKernel, 4 components, hidden 32) fitted by fit_em through exact BP on E03's exp31-train chains, 16 seeds x sizes (32, 128, 512, 2048). Iteration caps MATCHED at 1200 for both arms, which is what made E25's answer readable. e03._cell_common, e03._bundle, e03._sq, e03._risk and e03._one_view_groups are IMPORTED, not copied, so the bundles are the same objects the nets were scored on rather than a reconstruction that agrees. E03 hands the nets (X, t) pairs and fit_em wants (X, alpha, delta); alpha_delta(t) is that change of variable exactly, so the kernel arms train on the same corrupted sample the score nets trained on. Risk is recorded per level as well as pooled, because E28 found the pooled scalar hides a crossover. Part `verify` is the gate: E30's own sq_ref per (seed, n_chains, t) against E28's and E29's, since sq_ref depends only on the test bundle and the schedule.

predeclared_predictions.P1: mdn beats every score-net architecture at its best rung, at every M. This is E25's registered 'sits between' hypothesis, finally testable. FALSIFIED by any architecture whose best rung beats mdn at any M. NOTE, LEFT IN DELIBERATELY: reading E25's mdn (0.1461 at M=128, exp34 bundles) beside E29's best net (0.1080, exp31 bundles) HINTS this is false. That arithmetic is invalid -- it is the very cross-bundle comparison this experiment exists to replace -- so it does not license editing the prediction. It is recorded so a confirmation cannot later be read as having been obvious.
predeclared_predictions.P2: em_bp beats mdn at every M, replicating E25's 64/64 on different data. If it does not replicate, E25's answer to Q6 was bundle-specific and Q6 REOPENS.
predeclared_predictions.P3: the ordering is em_bp < mdn < best net at every M. P1 and P2 are its two halves.
predeclared_predictions.P4: em_bp refitted on exp31 lands within 10% of E28's frozen E02a kernel evaluated on the same bundles. A larger gap says the E02a fit and a fresh fit are not interchangeable, which would matter for every E28 and E29 ratio already reported.

predeclared_analysis: joint.csv: risk_pooled and risk_level per (seed, n_chains, arm), joined to E29's ladder.csv on (seed, n_chains) to give one table containing em_bp, mdn and every architecture rung on one estimand. Headline numbers: (a) mdn/em_bp per M, against E25's 2.04-2.57 on exp34 bundles; (b) mdn against the best net rung per M; (c) E30 em_bp against E28's frozen E02a em_bp on the same cells. at_cap and converged to be read together, as in E25.

outcome.gate: PASSED, run in the right place. 1152 overlapping (seed, n_chains, t) cells against E28 and E29, worst RELATIVE sq_ref disagreement 0.000e+00. E30 is on their bundles. The confirmatory jobs themselves exited 2 because the gate compares against locally fetched outputs that are export-ignored from the deploy archive -- see N-30; all 128 cells ran and no data was lost.
outcome.P1: FALSIFIED, and not narrowly. The MDN does NOT beat every architecture: it is beaten by 13 rungs at M=32, 12 at M=128, 4 at M=512 and 9 at M=2048, and by bigru at EVERY size. best-net/mdn = 0.81 / 0.75 / 0.79 / 0.81, i.e. the best score net is 19-25% BETTER than the neural kernel at every dataset size. The invalid cross-bundle arithmetic recorded in the prediction hinted at this and it was right, which is why the hint was recorded rather than acted on.
outcome.P2: CONFIRMED and slightly strengthened. em_bp beats mdn in 64/64 cells, ratios 2.12 / 2.52 / 2.47 / 2.91 against E25's 2.04 / 2.24 / 2.28 / 2.57 on exp34 bundles. Q6's answer REPLICATES on different data and is not bundle-specific.
outcome.P3: FALSIFIED, because P1 fails. The ordering is NOT em_bp < mdn < nets. Measured on one estimand it is em_bp (25 par) < best net (~1,105-4,001 par) < mdn (1,516 par): the MDN is the WORST of the three.
outcome.P4: CONFIRMED, far inside the 10% predicted. A fresh em_bp fit on exp31 lands within +0.42% at M=128 and -0.17% at M=2048 of E28's frozen E02a K=8 kernel on the same bundles. The E02a fit and a fresh fit ARE interchangeable, which validates every E28 and E29 ratio already reported.
outcome.headline: The value is in exact BP with a PARSIMONIOUS kernel, not in neural parameterisation of the kernel. Putting a neural network in the kernel slot LOSES to putting a comparable network in the score slot; putting a 25-parameter mixture there wins by 1.72-2.34x. E25's registered 'intermediate model' hypothesis is wrong: the MDN is not between the nets and EM-BP, it is below both. Consistent with the three-axis capacity U-shape (N-28): validation picks K=2 for the mixture at M=32/128, about five parameters, so 1,516 is far past the optimum for this problem.
outcome.budget: Clean at M=32 and M=128 (at_cap: em_bp 0/16 and 1/16, mdn 0/16 and 2/16). At M=2048 mdn is at cap in 14/16 and em_bp in 9/16, so quote M=32/128 as budget-free.

amendment_extended_budget.why: E30's conclusion is a NEGATIVE result about the neural kernel, so the arm that a longer budget would help is the arm that lost. At M=2048 the MDN selected the last checkpoint in 14/16 cells and em_bp in 9/16, so the two largest sizes are not budget-free. Cases e30m-s* rerun ONLY M=512 and M=2048 with both caps raised 1200 -> 3600. M=32 and M=128 are already budget-free (mdn at_cap 0/16 and 2/16) and are what the conclusion is quoted from, so rerunning them would triple the work to change nothing.
amendment_extended_budget.predeclared: P1 the ordering em_bp < best net < mdn is unchanged at M=512 and M=2048 at 3x the budget. P2 the MDN improves more than em_bp does, because it is the arm still at cap, but not enough to overtake the best score net (best-net/mdn stays below 1.0). P3 if the MDN DOES overtake the best net at 3x the budget, then E30's ordering was a budget artefact at large M and must be restated as holding at M=32 and M=128 only -- which is the outcome worth knowing and the reason this is worth the CPU-hours.
